tech.summary: Apple quietly lowered the daily spending cap on AI models for its employees last month. Some engineers had their budgets cut from $300 to $200, and the company is planning further cuts for some engineering teams that may potentially reduce their daily allowances to as little as $100. Groups outside of engineering may have their limits reduced to $25 from $100. Employees say that few workers were using their full $300 daily allowances, making the previous limits unnecessarily generous.

Users can adjust the speed of GIFs, edit individual frames, and share them. GPT-Image-2.6 Flare and Sunburst are now available through the API.

tech.title: SpaceX's Starfall just went from secret to storefront
tech.summary: SpaceX has launched a commercial page for Starfall, a disk-shaped reentry capsule that can carry up to 1,000 kg of payload. The capsule can supply 1 kW of power and connect to the internet through Starlink, allowing researchers to pull data from experiments while in orbit instead of waiting for splashdown. It can be used for manufacturing, research, or testing and is aimed at biomedical customers, pharmaceutical companies, and materials science research. Starfall's timeline will depend on Starship - SpaceX is preparing for Flight 15, where it aims to catch both stages with the launch tower.

tech.title: Why pharma firms are going to Earth's orbit in search of new cancer drugs
tech.summary: Varda Space Industries' autonomous factories carry miniature laboratories in which materials can be processed without astronauts. Once the process is complete, a capsule separates from the spacecraft and returns to Earth. The company currently has three spacecraft simultaneously in orbit. Manufacturing in space has several advantages, one of the most important being microgravity. Varda plans to launch seven missions in 2027 and 10 in 2028.

tech.title: Rebuilding the global town square from scratch
tech.summary: The new version of X.com's web app was built by five engineers working with AI coding agents in under six months. It loads pages significantly faster than the old web app over slow connections, and it already serves logged-out users and the pages that search engines crawl. This post covers why X.com was rebuilt, how the new web app is being rolled out, and how the old and new apps compare today. It also looks at the performance work completed since logged-out traffic moved over.

tech.title: Voice is Underutilized
tech.summary: Voice is a natural modality that is underutilized. It is great for rambling at coding agents and for capturing context. There is a lot of ambient context that exists in conversations with a ton of downstream value. This post presents some use cases for voice as a way to interact with AI.

tech.title: AI on the Ballot

It makes the full mathematical development of the Stacks Project available as a single, machine-checked library that researchers and AI agents can import from directly into new formal proofs.

webdev.title: A thousand fewer paths to root
webdev.summary: OpenAI's autonomous security pipeline reproduced 1,724 Linux kernel vulnerabilities and generated exploits for 948 distinct local privilege escalation flaws at an API cost of $1.2 million. Agents handled discovery, runtime validation, exploit development, and candidate patches before human review and maintainer reporting. The research highlights why validation must check how an exploit succeeds, after some agents gained root through a different vulnerability than the one assigned.

webdev.title: How We Made clarity.js 4.5% Smaller Without Sacrificing Compatibility
webdev.summary: Microsoft reduced clarity.js by 1,257 gzip bytes through more than 50 automated change, build, measure, and test experiments. Named imports and minifier settings delivered savings, while extracting small helpers sometimes increased compressed size. A larger saving from modern JavaScript output could not ship because native async functions would break Angular sites that depend on Zone.js.

webdev.title: You'll need nerves of steel to work with AI agents
webdev.summary: Fast, cheap coding agents can create substantial review work by deleting unrelated code, missing requirements, and making tests pass without exercising the intended behavior. More than 100 hours with Cursor's Composer 2.5 exposed failures ranging from unsolicited edits to disabled schema validation and tests that bypassed API routes. Explicit rules and reference implementations did not reliably prevent repeated mistakes.

webdev.title: Agentic Technical Debt and Where Orchestration Belongs in AI Agent Architecture
webdev.summary: Agent systems accumulate debt when prompts and agent loops take responsibility for approvals, side-effect retries, and audit trails. A supplier invoice dispute illustrates how to divide ownership among the model, harness, durable execution, and an orchestration control plane. A single agent inside one application may need only its harness, while processes crossing systems need explicit ownership of recovery and approval.

webdev.title: Nobody here writes code by hand anymore
webdev.summary: An account of adopting coding agents at Intento traces the shift from small experiments to a team that delegates code generation and reviews the output. The key change was making documentation, architectural decisions, tasks, and production logs accessible to models. Earlier failures on an established codebase were attributed to missing context that lived in people's heads, rather than the age of the code itself.

webdev.title: Scale Postgres Past the Slowdown – and Get $1,000 in Credits
webdev.summary: Growing Postgres databases eventually hit a wall: queries slow, dashboards lag, and adding another database starts to feel inevitable. Tiger Data keeps Postgres fast as your data grows with time-series primitives, columnar storage, and automatic partitioning. No pipelines or second system needed. Get $1,000 in credits when you sign up for free.

webdev.title: Graphify
webdev.summary: Graphify turns code and supporting material into a queryable knowledge graph with paths between concepts and an interactive browser view. Code parsing uses local tree-sitter analysis without an LLM or vector store, while document and media interpretation can use a model. Edges distinguish explicit source relationships from inferred connections, making the graph's evidence easier to inspect.

webdev.title: faster-chrome-devtools-skill
webdev.summary: This agent skill and dependency-free Node CLI control Chrome directly through the Chrome DevTools Protocol. It supports accessibility snapshots, tab management, screenshots, and raw protocol calls without requiring a separate browser MCP server. Screenshots are written to files so agents can choose when to load them into context.

webdev.title: A new Go API for JSON
webdev.summary: Go 1.27 makes encoding/json/v2 and encoding/json/jsontext generally available, addressing behavior and performance constraints that could not be fixed within the old API. The new defaults reject invalid UTF-8 and duplicate object names, while the packages separate Go value conversion from lower-level JSON syntax processing.

webdev.title: DOOM's DNA
webdev.summary: This interactive study compares the original DOOM source with 43 descendants to explore what survives copying, porting, and translation. Structural fingerprints and call relationships can reveal ancestry even when names or source text change. In a blind test, a Go translation's functions were assigned to the correct game subsystem 60% of the time, compared with 20% for shuffled labels.

webdev.title: The PHP2Shell Vulnerability Heralds Cybersecurity Hell
webdev.summary: AI-assisted researchers turned a PHP crash bug reported in 2024 into a critical vulnerability capable of running arbitrary code on a server. Finding the exploit took two weeks, while four engineers spent two months developing a patch, illustrating the growing gap between discovering flaws and safely fixing them. Better funding for open-source maintainers, defensive AI tools, and formal verification could help close that gap.

infosec.title: Cyberattack on French plasma stores is enough to make your blood boil
infosec.summary: Attackers compromised a refrigeration supplier and altered cold-room settings at France's Blood Establishment, changing temperatures from -30°C to 110°C. EFS monitoring detected the changes. Staff controlled or isolated affected units and moved plasma and samples elsewhere. No blood products were lost. The incident follows European attacks on supermarket refrigeration, including defrost cycles that spoiled food. CERT-FR had urged remediation of vulnerabilities in Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers.

infosec.title: Philippine Migrant Worker Data Likely Leaked in 69GB Breach
infosec.summary: An unknown actor copied 27 SQL Server backup databases belonging to the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration in 24 minutes. The 69GB set includes migrant-worker records, contracts, accreditation data, and cashier and LandBank financial records. The attacker used GodPotato, SeImpersonate, and Impacket, then left logs and tools on an open Singapore staging server. The stolen backups have not appeared for sale, and the final destination remains unknown. Hunt.io notified CERT-PH and the Department of Migrant Workers.

infosec.title: mSecure Password Manager Warns Users to Secure Their Credentials
infosec.summary: mSeven notified users of its mSecure password manager that it detected suspicious activity related to the app. Per the message, mSeven warned users to secure their credentials, raising suspicions that it may not be encrypting credentials securely. In an audit conducted last year by Germany's Federal Office for Information Security, the password manager was flagged as not meeting the usual expectations of password managers.

infosec.title: Finding 40+ Vulnerabilities in Healthcare Software Serving More Than 100 Million Patients
infosec.summary: An AI-assisted review of OpenEMR produced 42 published security advisories, fixed in version 8.5.0 on 27 October 2026. The issues include three critical findings: local file disclosure through the PDF generator, SQL injection through patient-data field names, and another SQL injection. Other bugs exposed patient records, allowed portal credential replacement, and enabled administrator API impersonation through an impersonation chain that combined SQL injection and file disclosure to forge an OAuth bearer token, bypassing password and MFA checks.

infosec.title: Why Conventional Reputation Feeds Miss Software Supply Chain Attacks
infosec.summary: Conventional threat intelligence feeds and multi-engine scanners fail to detect most software supply chain attacks on day zero, exposing organizations to malicious package behavior for months after public disclosure. Research indicates that blind-spot rates for supply chain attacks in these reputation tools range from 70% to 90%. General-purpose security tools remain ineffective against these threats because they are designed to detect inbound perimeter probes rather than malicious package behavior.

infosec.title: You Had Me at “Hello”: Inside The Greeter, A Chinese‑Language Framework Targeting AI Infrastructure
infosec.summary: Era researchers tracked a Chinese-language framework, Greeter, exploiting Flowise's overrideConfig code-injection flaw (CVE-2024-58351) across seven honeypots from July to October. Each “hello” request delivered a different command through javascriptFunction, without changing the saved chatflow. The framework ran host reconnaissance, searched .env files, SSH keys, and Flowise encryption keys, probed AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud metadata services, and checked Docker socket access, Linux capabilities, persistence paths, and memory-based execution. Of 3,277 identifiable internet-exposed Flowise instances, 703 lacked authentication. 46 matched the honeypot's vulnerable conditions.

infosec.title: Sentra (Product Launch)
infosec.summary: Sentra provides cloud-native data security and governance. It finds and classifies data across cloud, SaaS, warehouses, knowledge stores, and file shares, maps access by users and agents, enforces least privilege, and automates remediation.

infosec.title: Grim Prompter
infosec.summary: Grim Prompter is a Claude Code and Codex skill that has a coding agent build a threat model from a repo and cite file-and-line evidence for every trust boundary, threat, and mitigation. It ships 36 architecture-specific workflows, from RAG and agentic AI to OT/ICS and smart contracts, and 29 method prompts covering STRIDE, PASTA, LINDDUN, and MITRE ATLAS. Saved JSON baselines let the agent review a branch diff against the existing model.

infosec.title: sapper-v2
infosec.summary: sapper-v2 is a multi-agent pentest harness that won the 634-team qualifier of Tencent Cloud's AI Attack-Defense Challenge, capturing 85 flags in eight unattended hours on 1B tokens where the runner-up burned 4.5B. A commander agent reads a shared fact graph and dispatches scouts, generals, and soldiers through tmux, with GLM-5.3 making decisions and the cheaper DeepSeek V4.1 Flash doing the volume work. It works with any agent CLI, including Claude Code and Codex, and the coordination layer is spun out as the general-purpose nvwabase project.

infosec.title: Securing Our Frontier Model Training Environment
infosec.summary: At the end of September, OpenAI embarked on a frontier model training pause to harden its training infrastructure against potential escapes. Beyond host-based sandboxing, OpenAI limits its model training environment's network access to strictly necessary internal services and an “offline internet” of cached search indexes and pages. OpenAI also spent billions of tokens red-teaming its training environment to find gaps in its hardening.

infosec.title: Verifying Apple Reference Images
infosec.summary: The Privacy Preserving Systems Lab released the first publicly available tool to verify Apple Reference Images captured using the new cryptographic authentication standard for the iPhone 18 Pro series. The system utilizes secure camera hardware alongside Apple's Private Cloud Compute infrastructure to cryptographically sign pixel data. The protocol embeds a developer-accessible reference image next to the main photo using JUMBF boxes, SHA-512 hashing ranges, and a composite ML-DSA and RSA signature.

infosec.title: South Korea's Lee Calls For Powerful Government-Wide Cybersecurity Body
infosec.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung called for the creation of a powerful government-wide cybersecurity body to coordinate cybersecurity operations and response. In a cabinet meeting, Lee stated that the current system was too reactive and that a proactive system was needed to protect public services and critical infrastructure. Lee also stressed the need for further public- and private-sector collaboration.

infosec.title: Chainstack Reports Production Systems Breach Exposing Customer Data and Password Hashes
infosec.summary: Chainstack says an attacker entered via a third-party component on October 26 and reached production systems, accessing customer names, organizational details, email addresses, and password hashes.

infosec.title: Residential Proxies Detected on White House Network
infosec.summary: Proxy-detection vendor Layer3 Intel says its probes exited through the White House's own network (AS2650) 236 times in a month via 6 addresses and 28 commercial residential proxy services.

infosec.title: Frontline Education Data Breach Impacts Over 1.3 Million
infosec.summary: Hackers exploited a third-party software vulnerability on August 14 to access Frontline Education systems.

data.title: Frontier quality at 1% of the cost: a production benchmark of LLM classifiers
data.summary: Airbnb fine-tuned a model with 2 billion effective parameters to screen content for pricing-policy violations. Its F1 score rose from 0.563 to 0.902, matching the best frontier APIs, with a median latency of 35ms against their roughly 900ms. At thousands of requests a minute, the frontier models cost two orders of magnitude more than one self-hosted GPU.

data.title: Why we're moving our warehouse product off DuckDB
data.summary: Five months after rebuilding its warehouse product on DuckDB, PostHog is moving off it. Each instance had to be sized before the query arrived, and its DuckLake, holding about 1 trillion rows, could take over three minutes for a single-table write. PostHog is now rebuilding on Trino with its own table format, HogLake.

data.title: Upgrading Redshift from RA3 to RG and Achieving Faster Queries at 32% Lower Cost
data.summary: Halodoc migrated its Redshift warehouse from RA3 to Graviton-based RG instances after validating ingestion, ETL, dashboards, and governance compatibility. COPY operations ran roughly 6x faster, heavy reporting queries ran 2.1x to 5.2x faster, and queue times fell by around 70%. Overall Redshift costs dropped 32%, demonstrating the potential benefits of the new architecture for production analytics workloads.

data.title: F3 Lightning: How Meta Accelerates Ads ML Features to Production at Scale
data.summary: Meta rebuilt its ads ML feature infrastructure to deploy features independently without losing the efficiency of shared computation. F3 Lightning uses stable computation IDs, a unified execution plan, and shared memory to avoid redundant processing across more than 20,000 features. Comparable features now reach production 3.6x faster without increasing infrastructure compute costs.

data.title: The Great Data Interregnum - Morbid Symptoms of an Industry Between Eras
data.summary: The data industry is caught between vendor consolidation, AI-driven automation, and unresolved operational problems. Generating SQL, pipelines, and documentation is becoming cheaper, but broken data, inconsistent business definitions, and unclear accountability remain. The lasting value of data teams lies in semantics, governance, and understanding rather than producing more technical artifacts.

data.title: As Humans Write Less Code: Workloads Shift from Human to Agent Verification with Iterative Test Suites
data.summary: As AI agents generate more SQL, transformations, and dashboards, verifying their output becomes more important than writing the code itself. What dev teams really need are compiler-style validation, layered test suites, and unified lineage across data models and BI assets. Moving assertions earlier in development could make agent-generated analytics easier to audit and less prone to semantic drift.

data.title: Exploratory Data Analysis Can't Be Automated Away
data.summary: Exploratory data analysis still needs human eyes on the data. What looks weird depends on what you intend to do, which no model can know in a vacuum. LLMs rarely make the work faster.

data.summary: A new report by Datadog , based on the experiences of 109 data engineering practitioners, reveals the speed in which AI is expanding the data engineer's role, and why many teams feel unprepared. data.title: Helix Foundry: Turning Enterprise Data into an AI-Generated Knowledge Graph
data.summary: Helix Foundry connects databases, SaaS applications, and files, then uses an AI agent to propose an ontology and load the resulting entities and relationships into HelixDB. The open-source project supports local deployment and is adding consistent PostgreSQL snapshots and graph computation capabilities.

data.title: SurrealDB 4
data.summary: SurrealDB 4 rebuilds the query engine with 240+ fixes. It reports 42% faster CRUD operations and projects 22x faster indexed queries, while adding PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MongoDB compatibility. The same engine powers Earth's serverless databases on Cloudflare and SurrealDS' distributed clusters, which confirm writes only after storing them across two zones.

data.title: Apache Hudi-rs 0.6.0: Native Writes from Rust and Python
data.summary: Apache Hudi-rs 0.6.0 introduces native write support for Rust and Python, allowing applications to create, append, update, upsert, and delete records without Spark or a JVM. Its record-level index enables sub-second small-batch updates on tables containing millions of rows. The release also improves Python read performance by up to 6x while maintaining compatibility with existing Hudi query engines.

data.title: Scaling Model Evaluation at Pinterest with Ray (Part 4)
data.summary: Pinterest used to run inference with Ray, write predictions to S3, then start a Spark job to read them back and compute metrics. Its new evaluation platform computes partial metrics batch by batch inside the Ray inference job and combines them at the end. That cut end-to-end evaluation time by up to 32% for feature-importance runs.

data.title: RocketRide: A C++ Pipeline Engine for AI Workflows
data.summary: RocketRide is an open-source AI pipeline engine built around a multithreaded C++ runtime with more than 50 Python-extensible processing nodes. It supports multiple LLM providers, vector databases, and agent frameworks, with debugging and deployment tools integrated into VS Code.

design.title: Canva to Cut More Than 1000 Jobs in ‘Hardest Moment' of Its History
design.summary: Canva is restructuring 1,271 roles, affecting 22 percent of its workforce, after its growth slowed this year for the first time in a decade. Chief executive Melanie Perkins called it the hardest moment in Canva's thirteen-year history, announcing a merged product organization with fewer management layers. Departing staff receive at least six months' salary, and the cuts follow Canva slashing its own valuation to US$31 billion.

design.title: iOS 27.3 and macOS 27.3 add Vertical Tabs, Adaptive Dark Mode, and more to Safari
design.summary: Apple is introducing vertical tabs in Safari's developer betas across iPhone, iPad, and Mac, with tabs displayed as compact icons in a left sidebar that can expand to show website titles. A new Adaptive Dark Mode can automatically generate dark versions of websites that lack native support, either on demand or through a persistent preference. Siri AI can also organize, sort, move, and close tabs, with broader awareness of webpage content planned for a future update.

design.title: Agents struggle with the same bad UX we do
design.summary: Computer-use AI agents frequently fail at the same confusing interfaces that frustrate humans, including ambiguous buttons, hidden menus, unexplained disabled states, and disruptive overlays. People often compensate for these problems by guessing, backtracking, or relying on experience, while agents expose the underlying design debt through repeatable failures that are easier to observe. Making interfaces clearer for agents through explicit labels, visible states, predictable interactions, and semantic structure can also improve accessibility and usability for people.

design.title: Everyone is building AI agents. Who's designing the stop button?
design.summary: AI agents introduce unpredictable behavior into products traditionally designed around explicit rules and known transitions, making it essential to distinguish where autonomy is useful from where reliability is mandatory. Products can let AI interpret intentions and construct workflows while using deterministic execution, visible uncertainty, confirmation steps, and clear recovery mechanisms to protect consequential actions. Designing effective agent experiences increasingly means defining boundaries around what AI may decide, when humans must intervene, and how users can understand, correct, or stop an autonomous process.

design.title: Why 10,000 experiments work better than 10,000 hours for designers
design.summary: Repeatedly practicing the same design skills can make someone better at their current job without developing the problem-framing, influence, and decision-making abilities required for more senior roles. Instead of relying on experience alone, designers can break career goals into microskills and run small experiments, such as opening every design review with a specific decision or presenting research findings themselves. A weekly reflection can help turn these experiments into deliberate professional growth without requiring organizational approval or major changes to existing workflows.

design.title: A Drawing Toolbar for React
design.summary: Drawesome is a drawing toolbar for React. Seven pens, an eraser, SVG and PNG export, and no dependencies beyond React.

design.title: A Figma Design System and React Library That Stay in Sync
design.summary: A unified Figma design system and React component library: 80+ components, 73 ready-made blocks, 18,500+ components and variants, and 950+ variables and styles.

design.title: Thought-Orb Loading Indicators for AI Interfaces
design.summary: Thinking Orbs are animated AI thinking and loading indicators for React.

design.title: Bad AI Doesn't Smell
design.summary: Like a bad survey, bad AI output gives no sign that it's wrong, but authority bias, truth bias, and algorithm appreciation make people trust it anyway. In user research, mistranscriptions, missed body language, misread sarcasm, and hallucinations can turn into confident, wrong insights. Someone who ran the research has to check any AI analysis, ideally used only as a sense-check after doing their own.

design.title: How Afternow put Kinetik's identity and four products into one system
design.summary: Afternow redesigned healthcare transportation platform Kinetik around painterly city landscapes inspired by the view from a car window, replacing conventional clinical imagery with a warmer visual language built from purple, deep greens, gold, salmon, and lavender. GT Alpina provides expressive editorial typography, DM Sans supports accessible product interfaces, and AI-generated landscapes are carefully art-directed with documented prompts to maintain consistency. The identity extends across four products through a shared design system containing more than 300 components and 2,000 screens, using tokens to adapt spacing, density, and accessibility for administrators, transportation providers, and elderly patients.

design.title: Tokenizer Mono
design.summary: Tokenizer Mono is an experimental typeface based on IBM Plex Mono that visualizes how language models split text into tokens, using OpenType features to highlight boundaries directly as someone types without running a tokenizer in JavaScript. Its 28 styles represent different tokenizers from OpenAI, Meta, Google, DeepSeek, and others, combining contextual glyph substitutions with built-in color palettes to approximate token boundaries. Most styles achieve roughly 98% agreement with real tokenizers in testing, demonstrating how advanced font technology can perform surprisingly complex text processing while revealing its limitations around line breaks, uncommon words, and tokenization algorithms.

design.title: Chrome's new menu search makes settings and bookmarks easier to find
design.summary: Google is testing a searchable three-dot menu in Chrome that lets users find browser commands, bookmarks, and recently visited websites without navigating through nested menus.

design.title: Dutch Digital Artist Creates the Most Warm, Ethereal Artworks You Will Ever Lay Eyes On
design.summary: Utrecht-based digital artist and animator Lois van Baarle, known as Loish, paints expressive female figures in soft, glowing light, rich color, and flowing hair and clothing.

design.title: Designing Product Demos People Can Actually Follow
design.summary: A product demo is a sequence of state changes, so clarity depends on how attention moves between steps rather than on polished screens.

marketing.title: Create, send and analyze video in the AI tools you're already using
marketing.summary: You've got the campaign, the targeting, the ads. You know what would make it even better? Personalized video. And with Vidyard MCP , it's just a prompt away... → Connect Claude / ChatGPT / Gemini / whatever AI tools you're already using to Vidyard. → Create and share highly engaging videos with the assets you already have. → Integrate video across your GTM with the full context that your AI already knows. 🎉 Try the MCP for yourself on a free plan 🎉 See what Vidyard MCP can do in 42 seconds .

marketing.title: Is B2B SaaS Still Blogging?
marketing.summary: An analysis of blog posts from 219 mid-market B2B SaaS companies found total publishing volume across 187 companies increased 37% YoY and 151% since ChatGPT launched. Half of companies published more posts this year while median output rose from 42 to 62 posts annually. 52% of posts were how-tos, explainers, or comparisons. Only 2.4% contained original research or perspectives. Posts were also 55% longer, and posts per author increased 73%.

marketing.title: ChatGPT has hit roughly 20% of Google Search volume
marketing.summary: OpenAI says ChatGPT search volume has reached roughly 20% of Google Search's volume, making it Google's biggest search competitor yet. The estimate counts prompts that trigger a web search and may not be directly comparable to Google's search figures. ChatGPT's growth is driving Google to expand AI features in Search. OpenAI also says users value ChatGPT's personalization and is considering expanding its use of ads.

marketing.title: He's done 852 B2B video ads, here's what the top 1% have in common
marketing.summary: The strongest B2B video ads are built for a viewer who will probably skip them. The brand name lands in the first 5 seconds, and the product appears one feature at a time as a simple input and output. Hooks name a specific, emotional problem, and benefits become a moment the viewer can picture instead of a promise of saved time. Each cut is made for its specific channel, with an exaggerated prop like a dusty onboarding binder to make it more memorable.

marketing.title: Created a Content Collab Formula to Drive Revenue & Newsletter Signups
marketing.summary: Content partnerships can drive newsletter growth without paid placements. Start by identifying newsletters with overlapping audiences and pitch data-backed research that fits their readers. Build the relationship before asking for promotional CTAs. Then actively promote each collaboration to make it worthwhile for both sides. One company attributes 60-70% of new newsletter signups to 3 recommendation engines that continue driving subscribers months after the original collaborations.

marketing.title: Your marketing team moves fast. Does your website?
marketing.summary: AI makes campaigns faster than ever – but updating the website still means developer tickets, agency handoffs, and weeks of waiting. Wix's Web Portfolio Modernization Guide reveals the phased path to faster launches without rebuilding. Learn how marketing teams are giving brands and departments more freedom to build/publish without giving up centralized governance. Get the guide

marketing.title: How to use Google Analytics for social media (GA4 setup + reports)
marketing.summary: Use GA4 to measure what happens after someone clicks a social media link by tracking website traffic, engagement, conversions, and revenue. Start by setting up key events for actions like form submissions, purchases, and signups, then add UTM parameters to every social link to identify the platform, campaign, and specific post generating traffic. Use GA4's Traffic Acquisition, User Acquisition, Landing Page, and Attribution reports to compare platform performance, evaluate landing pages, and understand how social contributes to conversions across the customer journey. Build a Looker Studio dashboard to track these metrics over time and report social media's contribution to leads and revenue.

marketing.title: HTML vs. XML Sitemaps for Ecommerce
marketing.summary: Ecommerce sites should use both XML and HTML sitemaps to improve page discovery, crawling, and indexing. XML sitemaps automatically list every URL intended for indexing, while HTML sitemaps provide users and search engines with links to important categories, subcategories, and site pages. HTML sitemaps can also strengthen internal linking and help reduce the number of pages that Google crawls but does not index. Neither replaces a well-organized site hierarchy or strong internal linking, but HTML sitemaps can serve as a temporary solution during site restructures.

marketing.title: The growth playbook everyone keeps using
marketing.summary: Growth teams keep recycling the same tactics, like price increases, upmarket moves, and big launches. Most have worked at some point, which is why they return every few years under new names. The trouble is that they're often used to avoid fixing what's broken in the product or the company. Tactics are easy to assign owners and report progress on, while core problems don't fit a quarterly roadmap. Strong growth leaders stand out by knowing which problems are worth solving, then picking tactics that fit.

marketing.title: Which Types of Mentions Correlate the Strongest with AI Visibility?
marketing.summary: Off-site brand mentions correlate with visibility in ChatGPT, AI Mode, and AI Overviews. Reddit mentions had the strongest correlation (0.75), ahead of general web mentions (0.70) and press coverage (0.67). Brands with 10X more Reddit mentions typically received 5.5X more AI mentions, while 10X more webpage mentions correlated with 3.7X more. These are correlations, not proof that mentions cause AI visibility.

marketing.title: AI agent messaging: What 1,014 software buyers want
marketing.summary: Describing an AI product as a team of specialized agents generates more purchase interest than describing it as a single agent. A survey of 1,014 software buyers found that team framing increased purchase intent by 6.3 percentage points compared to single-agent framing. However, calling a product an agent alone did not increase purchase interest and slightly reduced it. Buyers also perceived products described as multiple agents as harder to use, while perceptions of helpfulness and trustworthiness remained largely unchanged. The findings suggest that breaking a product into distinct functions can increase its perceived value through a psychological phenomenon known as the unpacking effect.

marketing.title: Personality is the new fuel for marketing
marketing.summary: Personality-led brands codify the rhythms of how they talk, so they stay recognizable in a social reply or a Super Bowl ad.

marketing.title: Canva Cut 1,271 Roles Without Blaming AI. ChatGPT is Still Eating its Free Tier
marketing.summary: Canva is betting on brand management as AI makes design creation easier and cheaper.

marketing.title: We Are Testing Ad Placements in Reddit Search Pages
marketing.summary: Half of Reddit users say the platform helps them discover something new, which makes its search pages a high-intent spot for ads.

founders.title: Reach 8 million tech professionals reading TLDR
founders.summary: Ads get ignored on social media but not in TLDR! Reach founders, operators and startup leaders where they actually pay attention. Learn more about sponsorship opportunities .

founders.title: The Top 1% of AI Spenders Stalled in Q3. So Did Anthropic's Dollar Growth
founders.summary: AI spend peaked in July. The top 1% of firms on Ramp spent less on AI per employee in September than in July. Anthropic added $5.4 billion in revenue in the third quarter, down from $6.8 billion in Q2. Adoption across all other firms is still rising.

founders.title: The Financial Engineering Essential for AI in 2027
founders.summary: AI labs are in a price war over tokens while the GPUs behind those tokens cost more to rent. Labs try to secure GPUs on multiyear contracts at $2 to $4 an hour, then pay up to $13 once that capacity runs out. An investor's analysis estimates that Anthropic's average GPU cost rose 82% in two quarters. Anthropic's $5 billion short-term compute bill in Q3 helped turn an operating profit back into a loss. The analysis predicts labs will push enterprise buyers into multiyear minimum commitments so their customer contracts run as long as their GPU leases.

founders.title: AI companies should own their metering, not the entire billing stack
founders.summary: Billing involves several distinct jobs. Teams without billing expertise risk making bad choices with lasting consequences. AI companies should own usage measurement, pricing logic, and customer balances, but use specialist software for invoicing and revenue recognition. The back office should own a shared model of customer agreements.

founders.title: Your customers don't just want an agent. They want agents
founders.summary: Calling a product a team of agents can make it sound more useful even when the features haven't changed. Irrational Labs showed 1,014 US software buyers the same product page with different agent labels and asked whether they'd buy it and what they'd pay. The team label raised stated purchase interest by 6.3 percentage points over a single agent, but it didn't significantly beat wording with no agent and didn't raise willingness to pay. Buyers also rated the team version harder to use, so the researchers recommend making each agent's separate job visible and keeping setup clear.

founders.title: How We Built Alloy, Firecrawl's Internal Design Harness for AI Agents
founders.summary: A simple sales sheet could sit in Firecrawl's design queue for three or four days because the designer had other priorities. One of the company's product marketers built Alloy, an internal workspace that gives AI agents Firecrawl's brand rules and past approved work for each new asset. Editable product demos have been the biggest win, since changing wording or timing before launch no longer means recording the whole sequence again. The team has 63 reusable animation packages and says Alloy has saved days of work. Experiments stay on a canvas until someone deliberately publishes them for teammates.

founders.title: Cloudflare Personal Agent Controls
founders.summary: Track visiting AI agents and configure individual access policies for websites.

founders.title: Next Gen Zaps fix themselves when they break
founders.summary: Zapier Zaps now fix themselves when they break. An agent reads the error messages, works out a fix, tests it, and publishes a new version of the Zap. Changes are emailed to users. Small fixes will go through on their own - the agent will ask users before any big changes.

founders.title: Enterprise Managed Auth for connectors
founders.summary: Claude Enterprise Managed Auth lets organizations connect their users to MCP servers without sending each other through an OAuth consent screen. Claude presents authorization servers with an identity assertion and receives an access token after the assertion is validated. Existing access tokens remain valid until their specified lifetimes, even if a user is removed from the organization.

founders.title: Retire the word “context”
founders.summary: An agent with access to every Slack thread and call transcript at your company can still miss what you need done today. Linear's cofounder argues that storing more information still leaves someone to decide what the work is for and what a good result looks like. A useful briefing is short because someone chose what to leave out, so he recommends explaining why decisions were made and what the agent shouldn't change. Those answers need to stay current, since a six-month-old explanation can still look clear and credible after the team has changed direction.

founders.title: The Next Era of Notion
founders.summary: Agents are starting to use the same software your team does, and their needs can pull a product in a new direction. Notion's CEO says agents now create roughly half of Notion's pages, and MCP traffic from connected agents has grown about 60 times this year. He is steering Notion toward keeping company context up to date for other companies' agents as well as its own. Notion also moved finance reviews from monthly to several times a week to keep up with model releases.

founders.title: Copying Cope
founders.summary: Competitors used to wait until your product was obviously winning before they copied it. SuperMe's CEO watched rivals copy Grubhub and Pinterest years ago and says four venture-backed startups copied SuperMe in recent months, down to its navigation and custom icons. Copying is now cheap enough that rivals imitate a product before they know whether it's worth copying, so the CEO puts more weight on distribution and networks that keep growing once the products look alike. Grub Canada once copied Grubhub's HTML outright but couldn't copy the restaurant network behind the site.

founders.title: The story behind the billboard
founders.summary: Notion is behind the billboard with a row of app icons floating over the moon and no tagline.

founders.title: Critical thinking when agents do the work
founders.summary: An agent's summary of finished work can hide requirements it reinterpreted, so ask it to list the decisions it made for you.

founders.title: Some reasons SaaSpocalypse might not be as bad as we thought
founders.summary: AI lowers the barrier to entry for coding, but it doesn't remove it.

crypto.title: French bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa likely exploited for over $133 million
crypto.summary: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa reportedly lost over $133M from centralized exchange accounts, withdrawn as USDC and USDT. The attacker (unknown) is swapping USDC to ETH, using instant exchanges, converting to XMR and bridging. Possible OTC activity could push losses higher. The bank hasn't confirmed or denied the exploit, so the claims are unverified.

crypto.title: Morgan Stanley tokenizes US equities and Treasurys with DTCC
crypto.summary: Morgan Stanley tokenized US equities and Treasurys using DTCC's new service, which opened last week with 20 participants, including JPMorgan, Citi, Bank of America, Barclays, BNP Paribas, Fidelity, State Street, and UBS. DTC holds $114T in custody, and the service was built with input from 150+ firms, initially supporting Canton and a private Besu network. Morgan Stanley now expects tokenized equities on its ATS in Q1 2027, later than its prior H2 2026 target. NYSE/ICE are also building a tokenized trading platform, with Broadridge, Computershare, Equiniti, and Superstate signed as transfer agents.

crypto.title: Solar: Paradigm's 100x Faster Solidity Compiler
crypto.summary: Paradigm's Solar is a new Solidity compiler that compiles contracts over 100x faster than Solc, the current standard. Beyond compilation speed, Solar produces more EVM-efficient bytecode than Solady without requiring inline assembly, reducing on-chain execution costs for deployed contracts. The compiler also resolves the Stack Too Deep error, a long-standing constraint that forced Solidity developers to restructure code or rely on workarounds. Solar is available now via Foundry: run foundryup, then forge --use solar.

crypto.title: Mastercard and OpenAI Build the Payment Rails for AI Agents
crypto.summary: Mastercard formalized a strategic partnership with OpenAI anchored by a four-product agentic commerce stack addressing payment trust, agent trust, ecosystem trust, and merchant discoverability. The four products are Agent Pay (tokenized payments for AI agents), Verifiable Intent (buyer authorization capture), Agentic Trust Intelligence (bank and merchant risk scoring for AI-initiated transactions), and Agent Connect (merchant discovery by AI agents). Shopify's Shop Pay is among the first live deployments. Mastercard is betting on network tokens over one-time virtual card numbers as the core primitive. Visa, Stripe, and PayPal are building parallel infrastructure. Holiday shopping is expected to be the first high-volume stress test for agentic payment rails at scale.

crypto.title: Crypto Protocols Are Winning the AI Inference Price War
crypto.summary: Centralized inference providers face structural pricing floors tied to manual approval gates, regional electricity costs, and capital-market margin requirements, creating an opening for permissionless crypto routing layers. Surplus lets holders of excess API credits from OpenAI, Anthropic, and DeepSeek sell at a discount for USDC with no KYC, posting 57x token growth (10B to 570B tokens/day) and 78x request growth (143k to 11.2M/day) over the past 90 days. Engy runs a global miner competition on hardware and electricity efficiency, growing from 2.7B to 153B tokens/day while buyback-directed revenue climbed from $363 to $8,000/day in the same window. With the inference market at $160B/year and projected to reach $350B, autonomous AI agents consuming 5x more tokens than humans will concentrate purchasing power in the cheapest available providers, positioning these protocols to capture a growing share of AI compute spend as agent usage scales.

crypto.title: SEC Token Taxonomy FAQ Clarifies Decentralization Standards for Builders
crypto.summary: The SEC released a new FAQ expanding its token taxonomy framework, drawing on three clarifications flagged by a16z crypto General Counsel Miles Jennings. Q 1.4 confirms that projects can maintain decentralized governance while using legal entities like DUNAs (Decentralized Unincorporated Nonprofit Associations), resolving a structural question teams have faced when adding off-chain legal wrappers to on-chain protocols. Q 1.5 draws a formal line between permissioned and permissionless systems, and Q 1.6 separates "functional" tokens from tokens that qualify as investment contracts under securities law. Builders now have clearer criteria from the SEC to determine whether their protocol architecture and token design fall outside the agency's jurisdiction.

crypto.title: Agentic commerce overhyped today; underhyped for the next 3-6 months
crypto.summary: Agentic commerce is overhyped on current usage but will be underhyped on volume within 3-6 months, and products not optimized for agents will be left behind. Agents still fail often (browser use is slow and buggy, and credentials and payments carry friction), so 99% of consumers churn at the first issue. Most consumers outside SF don't use agents at all, and current products mainly serve high-income, tech-forward users. Growth will likely come from ChatGPT (1.2B weekly users) as it adds a wallet and in-chat purchases, with early data showing AI-driven traffic converts better than non-AI traffic.

crypto.title: Kamino's No-Equity Model Tests If Value Accrual Is DeFi's Last Moat
crypto.summary: Kamino Finance has structured $KMNO to eliminate the equity/token split that has drained value from most DeFi protocols: the Kamino Foundation holds all IP and captures 100% of revenue, including institutional deals, with $KMNO as the sole ownership layer and no separate equity class for founders, investors, or the team. CEO WeiszM committed $20M over two years to expand Kamino into banks, brokerages, and wallets, with his personal allocation vesting only if $KMNO hits and holds a series of valuation milestones rather than on a standard time schedule. This is a direct answer to the bank tokenization challenge posed by products like StanChart's tokenized deposits in Hong Kong: banks can earn spread from on-chain infrastructure but cannot structurally route that upside to depositors, while a foundation-owned revenue model can. User-owned value accrual, not openness or permissionlessness, is DeFi's defensible moat as traditional finance moves on-chain.

crypto.title: Agentic commerce is built only for buyers, and sellers have no agent
crypto.summary: Commerce has two parties, but agentic tools serve only the buyer.

crypto.title: Agentic commerce fails today because of hacky payment models
crypto.summary: Most people find agentic commerce doesn't work because agents pay through virtual cards or raw 16-digit card numbers.

crypto.title: Hyperliquid Policy Center Opens Summer 2027 Law Internships
crypto.summary: Hyperliquid's DC-based policy advocacy arm is recruiting rising 2L and 3L law students for Summer 2027 internships focused on the legal and regulatory questions around onchain markets access.

crypto.title: CZ calls for crypto security alliance as AI-driven attacks accelerate
crypto.summary: CZ said AI is speeding up attacks and firms should invest in AI defenses.

fintech.title: No Risk No Reward? When It Comes to AI, Financial Services Customers Beg to Differ
fintech.summary: Handling clients' money invites scrutiny. With AI now used in credit, fraud detection, compliance monitoring, and customer service, one unchecked hallucination can cost you an account. Fortunately, Seekr gives risk, compliance, and operations teams continuous observability, plain-language explainability, and a defensible audit trail for every decision. Learn how financial institutions use Seekr to: Trace every AI-assisted decision to the data and reasoning behind it. Test models against their own portfolio data and risk thresholds before deployment. Keep customer data in their own cloud, on premises, or air gapped. Accounting firm Stephano Slack is already putting this into practice. Watch how they've partnered with Seekr to build trusted AI agents for 401(k) audits.

fintech.title: Stripe Treasury launches in the UK
fintech.summary: Stripe, the programmable financial services company, today launched Stripe Treasury in the UK, enabling founders to manage money from the same Dashboard where they already accept payments, without navigating across separate providers.

fintech.title: Revolut's valuation jumps 53% to $115B ahead of planned US bank launch
fintech.summary: Revolut completed a secondary share sale at a $115 billion valuation, up 53% from a year earlier, as it prepares to launch a US national bank in the first half of 2027 pending final approval. The company now serves more than 80 million retail customers, while Revolut Business generates about $1.28 billion of annualized revenue and processes roughly $48.6 billion of transactions each month, giving the company another major growth engine as it considers a potential IPO no earlier than 2028.

fintech.title: Sequoia rewinds 20 years of expansion to refocus on concentrated venture investing
fintech.summary: Sequoia is simplifying its organization after two decades of expansion, shutting its London office, ending the Arc accelerator and Scouts program, merging early-stage and growth investing, flattening the partnership, and eliminating its Monday partner meeting. The firm says it has raised about $10 billion of new capital and is returning to a more concentrated model built around fewer bets, a smaller team, and deeper support for founders from its Bay Area base.

fintech.title: NetSuite founder says “ERP as we know it is over”
fintech.summary: AI will change ERP more profoundly than cloud computing by shifting software from a system people operate into one that understands business context and increasingly performs work on their behalf. NetSuite is pushing this through NetSuite Next, MCP-based AI connectors and SuiteSkills, industry-specific agents, faster AI-assisted implementations, and an “Autonomous Suite” where agents handle tasks such as reconciliations, approvals, and close exceptions while staying within existing permissions and controls.

fintech.title: Payments are the new ads
fintech.summary: The one-time virtual cards behind most agent purchases today are a fragile bridge, breaking rewards, purchase protection, and checkout flows, while banks hold off on issuing agent network tokens until liability is settled. Meanwhile, agent platforms are routing around banks with prefunded stablecoin balances, where the bank sees one top-up and the platform earns roughly 4x more per $100 than on a virtual card. As agents erode ad revenue, platforms like Meta (charging fees on Muse-completed sales) will turn to payments to monetize, and banks risk losing the customer unless they step in to own agent liability.

fintech.title: Sweat the Details: Why good payments get declined and how to optimize fraud, cost, and acceptance
fintech.summary: Payment optimization is a three-way trade-off between fraud, cost, and acceptance, with small differences in issuer behavior, routing, authentication, and payment data often determining whether a legitimate transaction succeeds profitably. Optimize for net business outcome rather than one metric in isolation, using detailed payment data and issuer-specific knowledge to reduce fraud, lower fees, and recover good transactions without creating new losses.

fintech.title: From Equity to Possibility: Plan Before the IPO
fintech.summary: An IPO can bring new possibilities—and new decisions—while you stay focused on building. J.P. fintech.title: Revolut secures New Zealand banking license, expanding its global footprint
fintech.summary: Revolut now holds seven bank licenses, five secured this year, and operates as a licensed bank in 34 geographies.

fintech.title: OnePay introduces stablecoin deposits powered by Stripe
fintech.summary: Starting today, select customers in the US can use stablecoins to fund their OnePay Checking and receive the value as US dollars. Send stablecoins from an external wallet to a deposit address, and they are converted to US dollars and credited to your Checking balance within moments, with no conversion fees at launch.

fintech.title: Mastercard expands HDFC partnership to scale in India
fintech.summary: Mastercard expanded its partnership with HDFC Bank, India's largest private bank, with a new small-business agreement that could support roughly 3 million additional cards and more services sold through HDFC's 100 million-customer base. The strategy is to grow alongside India's UPI system, betting that greater digital-payment adoption will eventually push more consumers and businesses toward debit, credit, and other Mastercard products.

fintech.title: Pine Lab brings unified commerce to Singapore with Stripe
fintech.summary: Leading merchant commerce platform Pine Labs and global programmable financial infrastructure provider Stripe today announced a unified commerce solution that enables eligible retailers in Singapore to manage online and in-store payments through a single platform, simplifying operations while helping retailers engage customers more effectively across online and in-store channels.

fintech.title: API-Driven Commerce: How Programmable Money is Automated for Modern B2B Marketplaces
fintech.summary: B2B marketplaces routinely process transactions involving three suppliers, four tax jurisdictions, net-60 terms, and a platform take-rate. Handling these payment flows via batch processing or manual finance ops creates immediate bottlenecks. Moving money across complex seller networks requires treating currency as software logic rather than static banking entries.

fintech.title: AI financing drives private credit growth as refinancing risks rise
fintech.summary: AI infrastructure is expanding private credit beyond traditional corporate lending into land, power, semiconductors, and compute, with hyperscalers and CoreWeave expected to spend nearly $1 trillion in 2027 using cash flow, debt, joint ventures, and SPVs. The risk is a large refinancing wall from 2027 to 2029, especially for weaker borrowers using PIK interest, while increasingly circular financing between chipmakers, AI developers, and infrastructure providers could create correlated losses in a downturn.

fintech.title: Is Private Equity Cooked?
fintech.summary: PE-backed tech exit value is down 77% from a year ago, and roughly $140 billion of risky PE-backed loans mature in 2028 and $160 billion in 2029, about a third of it software.

fintech.title: Anthropic reports $17B of Q3 revenue as compute commitments approach $900B
fintech.summary: Anthropic reported about $17 billion in Q3 revenue, bringing nine-month revenue to $33.24 billion, up roughly 1,200% year over year, though sequential growth slowed to 47% from much faster rates earlier in the year.

fintech.title: Does taxing the rich work?
fintech.summary: Tax policy should encourage productive investment, with economic outcomes depending on how both governments and businesses use capital.

it.title: StackAI is the AI workflow automation platform that won't cause IT nightmares

Deploy anywhere (on-premise, multi-tenant, etc.) 2/ Seamless, intuitive building: No-code canvas = every team can build powerful workflows, while IT keeps full oversight 3/ Cutting-edge features: Human-in-the-loop, computer use, browser automation = AI agents that log into legacy systems, write files, execute code 4/ White-glove support: AI experts + engineers optimize every use case, so CIOs get the fastest time to value (3 months!) See StackAI in action today →

it.title: CrowdStrike introduces a kill switch for AI agents
it.summary: CrowdStrike's new AI Kill Switch lets security teams block agents' access to AI models through connected gateways. Broader controls, including terminating endpoint processes and revoking agent permissions, remain in development.

it.title: VMware returns to smaller deployments with vSphere Express
it.summary: Broadcom introduced vSphere Express for deployments of up to 128 processor cores, giving smaller customers an alternative to its larger VMware bundles. It includes live VM migration, automated recovery, and distributed switching, although individual installations cannot be managed centrally.

it.title: Accelerating engineering for the physical world
it.summary: OpenAI is sharing advances in how its models help engineers design, simulate, and build physical products across mechanical and electrical engineering. In an internal test, the company used GPT-6 Astra to define requirements and design the enclosure, printed circuit board, and software integrations for a device without direct human edits. Additionally, OpenAI is working with industry collaborators such as Chip Ganassi Racing and Mazda to test these capabilities on real-world engineering and prototyping problems.

it.title: Disconnected AI projects are multiplying enterprise costs
it.summary: Separate departmental AI projects create hidden costs through duplicate platform purchases, repeated data preparation, and unmonitored model usage. Maintain a shared inventory of tools and pilots, then compare each project's operating costs against its measurable benefits.

it.title: What does disaster recovery look like in an AI-centric world?
it.summary: As businesses increasingly rely on AI as operational infrastructure, outages and dependencies outside direct control highlight the need to update disaster recovery strategies. Experts suggest defining a minimum viable company that includes AI models, RAG data, and identity dependencies, while accounting for non-deterministic model outputs and fast-acting autonomous AI agents.

it.title: Business Ontology: Governed Context for AI
it.summary: Snowflake has announced the upcoming public preview of Business Ontology, a new business modeling and governance layer within Snowflake Horizon Context designed to provide AI agents with governed business context. The feature allows organizations to define concepts, metrics, and relationships, linking them to underlying semantic views to ensure AI models rely on approved enterprise definitions. Snowflake also helped found Apache Ossie, an open-source standard for semantic models to enable interoperability across tools.

it.title: Otari by Mozilla AI: your operating system for AI governance
it.summary: Mozilla AI has launched Otari, an open-source operating system and gateway designed for AI governance and multi-provider choice. The platform allows organizations to enforce tool restrictions, manage user budgets, and trace AI sessions in one place, while enabling seamless switching between model providers through a single API config change.

it.title: Adobe brings customer experience agents into major AI platforms
it.summary: Adobe's CX Enterprise Coworker is now available within ChatGPT, Claude, Databricks Genie, Gemini for business, and Microsoft Copilot. The integrations let marketers retrieve data and coordinate customer experience tasks across connected systems, with AWS, IBM, and Snowflake support planned.

it.title: MongoDB brings live Atlas data into Microsoft 365 Copilot
it.summary: MongoDB's generally available Atlas connector lets Microsoft 365 Copilot answer questions using live operational data. The integration uses a managed MCP server to query Atlas directly, allowing users to investigate orders, incidents, and business metrics without relying on a static data copy.

it.title: Seamless graph intelligence for your Snowflake data estate: The Neo4j and Snowflake partnership
it.summary: Neo4j and Snowflake have partnered to integrate Neo4j's graph intelligence capabilities into the Snowflake AI Data Cloud, aiming to improve AI reasoning and enterprise data insights without time-consuming ETL processes. The partnership introduces three core deployment options: Virtual Graph for zero-data-movement querying, Graph Analytics for Snowflake for on-demand SQL-based graph algorithms, and AuraDB integration for real-time mission-critical workloads.

it.title: Microsoft rounds up Windows management changes and upcoming deadlines
it.summary: Microsoft's latest IT roundup covers Windows recovery improvements and Intune controls that let standard users change approved network settings without broader admin access. It also flags Windows Update certificate expirations in 2027 and the January 15 end of CNAME-based discovery for Windows MDM-only enrollment.

it.title: Google unveils $15 billion data center investment in Malaysia
it.summary: Google announced a $15 billion investment in Malaysia over the next two years to build data centers and other infrastructure to support surging demand for artificial intelligence services.

it.title: Confluent introduces Streamhouse for real-time business context
it.summary: Confluent's Streamhouse architecture combines streaming, processing, governance, and querying to give applications and AI agents a continuously updated view of business operations.

it.title: IBM launches managed HashiCorp Vault on dedicated infrastructure
it.summary: IBM Cloud Secrets Manager Vault Dedicated offers single-tenant Vault Enterprise deployments with IBM handling infrastructure and operations, alongside dynamic credentials, automated rotation, and policy-based access.
